subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which structure follows the pattern ABA?
questions.explain: Ternary form has three sections in an ABA pattern, where the A material returns.

options: A single melodic line with no accompaniment
questions.explain: Monophonic texture is a single unaccompanied melodic line.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is a:
questions.explain: C up to G spans five letter names, making a perfect 5th.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'staccato' tells a player to make notes:
questions.explain: Staccato means short and detached, the opposite of legato.

questions.q: Which cadence ends on chord V, sounding unfinished?
questions.explain: An imperfect cadence ends on chord V and sounds incomplete.

questions.q: What does the time signature 3/4 tell you?
options: Four beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Three beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Three beats in a bar, each a quaver
questions.explain: In 3/4 there are three crotchet beats per bar, giving a waltz feel.

questions.q: A rondo form is best described by which pattern?
questions.explain: In rondo form a main theme (A) returns between contrasting episodes, e.g. ABACA.

options: Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together
questions.explain: Polyphonic texture combines two or more independent melodic lines.

questions.q: In music, what does the dynamic marking 'forte' (f) mean?
questions.explain: Forte is an Italian dynamic term meaning loud, while piano means quiet.
Ritardando means to gradually slow the tempo down.

questions.q: What does a 'crescendo' instruct a performer to do?
questions.explain: A crescendo is a gradual increase in volume, opposite to a diminuendo.

options: Placing accents on weak or off beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses normally weak beats or off-beats, disrupting the regular pulse.
